items.title: Implement CP-0 read-only global control inventory report
items.context: Produce a non-mutating report joining lifecycle, authority, readiness, proof diagnostics where available, active story titles, and queue classification. It must name authoritative cwd for worktree stories and avoid plan-doc heuristics.
items.userSees: The JSON output contains "schemaVersion":"lattice.global_control_status.v1", "readOnly":true, "authoritativeCwd":"/Users/.../.worktrees/B-xxxx", and "queue":{"classification":"..."} for each active story.

happy.desc: global_control_status returns schemaVersion, readOnly=true, project summary, and story rows including authoritative cwd for worktree stories.

edge.desc: A story with worktree authority and main mirror drift reports the worktree authoritative cwd instead of trusting stale main metadata.

adversarial.desc: The report does not mutate story metadata, process events, evidence, or git status.

verificationEvidence.note: Smoke asserts global_control_status schemaVersion/readOnly and story rows with authoritative worktree cwd and queue classification.
Smoke creates a main mirror INIT_CHECK / worktree DEV drift story and asserts authoritativeCwd points to the worktree.
Smoke snapshots git status before read-only commands and asserts global/runtime/waterline/queue reads leave git status unchanged.

items.title: Implement CP-1 runtime closure projection
items.context: Project runtime readiness from existing shipped modules only: story authority, owner lease, main write lock, validation lock, freshness hints, lifecycle readiness, and done_prepare bindings. Do not create a second freshness classifier.
items.userSees: The runtime row prints "runtime":{"status":"yellow","source":"runtime-projection","nextSafeAction":"cd /Users/.../.worktrees/B-xxxx"} when authority is in a story worktree.

happy.desc: runtime_closure_status projects authority, lock/readiness, stale evidence hints, and nextSafeAction from existing runtime modules.

edge.desc: Self-reentry or active validation lock is rendered as active/wait instead of a foreign-host conflict.

adversarial.desc: Runtime projection does not reclassify freshness differently from the shipped evidence freshness/readiness classifier.

verificationEvidence.note: Runtime closure smoke and CLI run project authority, locks, readiness rows, and nextSafeAction from shipped modules.
Smoke covers runtime projection over a worktree-authoritative story and status output distinguishes validation lock self-reentry in projector API coverage.
Runtime projector consumes lifecycle_check/story_authority_resolve/freshness surfaces and process-fact contract confirms no new proof or lifecycle gate fact replaces existing classifiers.

items.title: Implement CP-2 consumption closure projection
items.context: Consume Proof Admissibility public APIs or equivalent diagnostics to render consumer weakness without recalculating proof policy. Candidate, diagnostic, and legacy evidence must not satisfy DONE.
items.userSees: lattice admissibility_waterline --storyId=<id> --format=json shows each consumer bucket, missing clauses, top reasons, stale/legacy/error counts, and the consumption section uses that waterline without letting candidate, diagnostic, or legacy evidence satisfy DONE.

happy.desc: admissibility_waterline renders consumer pass/warn/fail/error/stale/legacy buckets, missingClauses, topReasons, and diagnostic-only status.

edge.desc: Historical failed or stale rows remain visible for audit but do not block unrelated stories without current subject/consumer/contract/material/policy match.

adversarial.desc: Candidate, diagnostic, and legacy artifacts cannot make DONE or production wording eligible through either admissibility_waterline or global_control_status.

verificationEvidence.note: Smoke and CLI assert admissibility_waterline schema, consumer rows, missing clauses, top reasons, stale/legacy/error/fail counts, and diagnosticOnly=true.
Waterline rows are story-scoped diagnostics; stale/historical rows remain visible without becoming unrelated story blockers.
Smoke and CLI assert diagnosticOnly=true and productionDoneEligible=false for DONE/consumer rows, so candidate/diagnostic/legacy artifacts cannot satisfy DONE through the waterline or dashboard.

items.title: Implement CP-3 queue governance and experiment exceptions
items.context: Classify active stories, add durable experiment exception registry, register Tier-C provider-execution receipt verification, exclude exceptions from duplicate cleanup, and keep malformed experiment stories visible.
items.userSees: The queue output contains "experimentBatches":[{"experimentBatchId":"tier-c-provider-execution-receipt-verification","defaultDashboardMode":"collapsed","storyCount":...}] and expanded mode lists member story ids.

happy.desc: queue_governance_status classifies active-worktree, stale-worktree, main-init, experiment-batch-exception, duplicate-candidate, superseded, and cleanup-required rows with collapsed and expanded views.

edge.desc: Tier-C provider-execution receipt verification stories are grouped and excluded from duplicate cleanup pressure while expanded view lists members.

adversarial.desc: Malformed experiment records are still visible as cleanup-required and are not hidden by the exception.

items.title: Implement CP-4 unified dashboard command output
items.context: Expose story-level and project-level control status so operators do not manually stitch session_brief, story_authority_resolve, proof diagnostics, and story list. Keep story gate status separate from project queue health.
items.userSees: The text dashboard shows "Project control status", "Story rows", "Runtime", "Consumption", "Queue", and "Next safe action" sections, with project queue warnings separate from story blockers.

happy.desc: global_control_status text and JSON render story-level and project-level sections with top blockers and next safe actions.

edge.desc: Project-level queue pressure does not mark an unrelated individual story gate as blocked.

adversarial.desc: The dashboard output cannot be derived from stale plan docs alone and includes source/status provenance fields.

items.title: Implement CP-5A runtime enforcement rollout guardrails
items.context: Hard-block only unsafe runtime operations named by the plan, with warn-first policy and rollback/config documentation. Runtime enforcement must not evaluate proof admissibility.
items.userSees: Unsafe runtime guard output contains "mode":"warn" or "mode":"enforce", "blocked":true, "reason":"wrong_authoritative_cwd", and "rollback":"set lifecycleControl.runtimeEnforcement=warn" for named unsafe cases.

happy.desc: Runtime enforcement guard blocks named unsafe runtime operations in enforce mode and renders warn mode before enforcement.

edge.desc: Metadata-only dirty state and material dirty state are distinguished in runtime guard output.

adversarial.desc: Runtime enforcement does not evaluate proof admissibility or implement Proof M7 policy.

items.title: Implement CP-5B queue governance guard and verification
items.context: Guard accidental duplicate/superseded mutations while preserving Tier-C experiment evidence. Exception writes must be auditable and guarded; non-experiment cleanup must be reviewable.

happy.desc: queue_exception_set records auditable exception membership with policyVersion, class, source, storyFilesHash binding, dashboard mode, cleanup policy, actor, reason, and timestamp.

edge.desc: Non-experiment duplicate cleanup emits reviewable canonical/superseded suggestions instead of silent mutation.

adversarial.desc: Tier-C experiment exception stories are never hard-blocked or cleaned up by duplicate guard logic, and malformed records remain cleanup-required.
